To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Chinese businesses in sectors under the watch of a developmental state, that are facing increasing competition from Western multinationals, and that lack offspring who are both competent and interested in taking over the family businesses have loosened family control.

(i) family-ruled businesses in Singapore shifted to becoming professionally managed family-ru led enterprises before the crisis; (ii) the shift was driven by the need to survive in the global economy and to take advantage of the opportunity of globalisation; and (iii) the family-ruled enterprise has been maintained in some sectors since the crisis, but has loosened in others.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how family businesses have responded to the Asian currency crisis, and what the implications of these changes are for the family, for the firm and for the state.
the role of the family and the state in the governance of family businesses.
how family businesses are managed, how the family business model is changing and why it is changing in Singapore.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Chinese family business in Singapore is a professionally managed family ruled enterprise.
the family business is not dead in Singapore.
family rule in Chinese family businesses is not a static concept.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
family firms are more likely to survive if they are able to adapt to the changing environment, and the state plays a crucial role in facilitating the adaptation process.
we have shown that family rule in Chinese family businesses in Singapore is not a static concept but is a process that is shaped by the interplay between the state, markets and corporate actors.
the family-ruled enterprise in Singapore has been a dynamic and flexible institution, which is capable of adapting to changes in the external environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the family enterprise has been a dynamic and adaptive institution, capable of adjusting to the changes in the external environment and internal management.
the management of family businesses is not a static process but one that is constantly changing and evolving.
the family enterprise is not an immutable institution, but one that is shaped and reshaped by its environment.
